request.spec:
Show the activity of the sheet: for every user and every event in the sheet's audit file, one
line <user> <EVENT> <count>, sorted by user then event.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show the activity of the sheet: for every user and every event in the sheet's audit file, one
line <user> <EVENT> <count>, sorted by user then event.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The sheet now has an Activity panel. Pressing **Show** reads the sheet's audit lines and lists one line per user and event, `<user> <EVENT> <count>`, sorted by user and then by event. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 acceptance tests.

- **Server:** I added `Audit.activity(sheetId)` in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/Audit.java`. It reuses the existing per-sheet line reader and takes the user from each line's `by=` field.
- **Endpoint:** `GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/activity`, defined in `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/sheets/{sheetId}/activity.GET.yml` and handled by the new `RespondWithActivity.java`.
- **Front end:** the panel is `src/main/frontend/features/auditView/activity.slot.tsx` and sits next to the existing Audit viewer. It uses the test's anchors: `activity-show` for the button and `activity-line` for each line, plus `activity-error` if the lines can't be read. Each press clears the old lines and reads the audit file again, so the counts are always current.

Users and events are sorted in plain character order, which puts capitalised names before lower-case ones. Showing the activity writes nothing to the audit file and changes no stored data.
